partner_context.their_ambition: Shun Tak operates TurboJET, the iconic high-speed ferry network linking Hong Kong, Macau and the Pearl River Delta — one of the world's busiest fast-ferry franchises, with the HK–Macau Outer Harbour service its backbone.
partner_context.their_pressure: The fleet is aging fuel-hungry diesel jetfoils and catamarans; the HK–Zhuhai–Macau Bridge has eaten ferry share; fuel and emissions are rising costs; and the network needs a modernization story to defend its franchise.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: A foiling fleet that runs the same HK–Macau–PRD routes faster, far more efficiently (10x vs planing) and near-silently — modernizing the franchise, cutting fuel cost and emissions, and competing with the bridge on speed and experience.

hero.title: The Pearl River Delta, on foils.
hero.subtitle: Modernizing the iconic HK–Macau–PRD high-speed ferry network with silent, efficient foiling vessels.
hero.what_we_do_together: Shun Tak / TurboJET bring the legendary Pearl River Delta ferry franchise, terminals and ridership; Navier brings the foiling fleet that runs the same network faster, cleaner and quieter — with dramatically lower fuel cost.

why_now: The TurboJET fleet is due for renewal, the HK–Zhuhai–Macau Bridge has pressured ferry share, and Hong Kong and Macau both have decarbonization goals — the moment to modernize the Pearl River Delta ferry network with foiling is now.
multimodal_fit: Shun Tak's terminals already integrate with HK's MTR, the airport and cross-border coaches; a foiling fleet runs the same berths and connections — faster and cleaner — within the existing intermodal network.

differentiation.why_navier: A software-defined, autonomy-ready foiling platform that runs the existing PRD network faster, ~10x more efficiently and near-silently — modernizing an aging diesel fleet with only berth-side changes, and competing with the bridge on speed and experience.

proof_points.claim: TurboJET is an iconic PRD fast-ferry franchise.
proof_points.evidence: One of the world's busiest fast-ferry networks, with HK–Macau its backbone.

proof_points.claim: The fleet is aging diesel jetfoils.
proof_points.evidence: Fuel-hungry, high-emission vessels due for renewal — a direct opening for an efficient foiling replacement.

proof_points.claim: The HKZM Bridge pressured ferry share.
proof_points.evidence: The bridge took cross-delta traffic; ferries need a faster, better-experience modernization to compete.

proof_points.claim: HK and Macau have decarbonization goals.
proof_points.evidence: Both cities target lower marine emissions, favoring efficient electric/hybrid foiling vessels.

objections.concern: The Pearl River estuary is busy and silty.
objections.response: Software-defined routing manages the heavy traffic and traffic-separation schemes; foils ride above the chop, and Quanta-LR hybrid suits the estuary distances.

objections.concern: The HKZM Bridge is the main competitor.
objections.response: Ferries win on city-center-to-city-center speed and experience; a faster, quieter, cleaner foiling fleet sharpens that edge precisely where the bridge is weak.

objections.concern: Fleet renewal is a major capital decision.
objections.response: We start with a pilot route (HK–Macau Outer Harbour) to prove fuel savings, speed and reliability before any fleet-wide commitment — de-risking the renewal.
Shun Tak's established franchise and terminals carry the cross-border framework; the foiling fleet operates within the existing licensed structure.

the_ask.navier_brings: The foiling fleet, captain training, maintenance and certification path, and the software-defined operating platform.
the_ask.partner_brings: Shun Tak / TurboJET bring the iconic PRD ferry franchise, terminals, cross-border framework, ridership and intermodal integration.
the_ask.together: A faster, cleaner, more efficient foiling fleet that modernizes the iconic Hong Kong–Macau–Pearl River Delta ferry network.

close.title: The Pearl River Delta, modernized.
close.body: A foiling fleet that runs the iconic HK–Macau–PRD network faster, cleaner and ~10x more efficiently — defending the franchise and decarbonizing the delta.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. That's the fundamental contrast with flying taxis and other new-infrastructure modes: nothing to permit, build, or wait for.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Fleet renewal pressure, HKZM Bridge competition, and HK/Macau decarbonization goals converge — a faster, far more efficient, near-silent foiling fleet modernizes the iconic Pearl River Delta network.

end_state.headline: A modernized, decarbonized Pearl River Delta foiling ferry network.
end_state.addressable_footprint: Hong Kong + Macau + Zhuhai + Shenzhen + HK Airport SkyPier — the PRD fast-ferry franchise.
end_state.narrative: TurboJET's iconic HK–Macau–PRD network runs on a foiling fleet — faster, near-silent and ~10x more efficient — defending the franchise against the bridge, cutting fuel and emissions, and modernizing one of the world's busiest fast-ferry networks.

revenue_potential.headline: The floor and the prize — every rung traces to grounded, sourced demand.
revenue_potential.modal_lead: We start from grounded corridor demand. Each step adds one realistic expansion lever — network width, induced demand, and journey wallet.
revenue_potential.anchor_note: $25M/yr premium sea-transfer spend on sourced corridors today — the anchor every rung builds from.

whose_money_legend.navier_transport_revenue: Fare the Navier boats collect. This is the corridor P&L (atom.py). SOM/SAM rungs are in this unit.
whose_money_legend.journey_gmv: Total guest journey spend across transport, food, stays, experiences, and ancillary revenue the partner monetizes on-island. Journey GMV rung is in this unit.

revenue_potential.cite_rule: Cite MID. 'High' stacks every optimistic assumption — ceiling, not headline.

rungs.label: SOM — floor (published)
rungs.basis: sourced flagship corridors · 10% capture · today's demand

rungs.label: SOM — full network
rungs.basis: whole mapped network · 10% capture · today's demand (no growth assumed)

rungs.label: SAM — matured network
rungs.basis: faster, more comfortable boats grow the market · leading-operator 25% capture, network-wide

rungs.label: Marine mobility TAM — induced marine-transfer market
rungs.basis: SAM divided by leading-operator capture — the full inducible water-transfer wallet at network maturity

rungs.label: Journey GMV — food + stays + experiences (≈3× TAM)
rungs.basis: add food, stays, and experiences to every crossing in the induced market

phase_economics.headline: Revenue potential by phase — conservative floor first, ecosystem prize last.
phase_economics.conversion_note: Fleet & CO2 scale from the grounded unit: 9 boats = $2.5M transport rev = 915 t CO2/yr (~$278K rev/boat).

horizons.fleet_note: Pioneer-equivalent; N35 mix lowers hull count for the same throughput.

vessel_sizing.headline: Right vessel for every leg — corridor range picks the hull.

classes.role: Capillary corridors ≤ 70nm. The workhorse of Prove + Scale.
Doubles throughput per hull on dense corridors; roughly halves payback. Scale-phase workhorse.
Regional legs 75–150nm beyond Pioneer range. Held out of near-term numbers.

vessel_sizing.range_gate_note: ≤ 70nm → Pioneer II (now). 75–150nm → Quanta-LR (roadmap). Long legs never faked on a 70nm boat.

_render_chip_flag.confidence_display: Tag every banded rung; lead with floor + corridor COUNT (ID-traceable). Never headline the 'high' band.

growth_case.modal_lead: We start from grounded corridor demand. Each step adds one realistic expansion lever — network width, induced demand, and journey wallet.
growth_case.modal_headline: Floor to prize — every rung traces to grounded demand

ladder_transitions.headline: Same 10% capture, expanded to the full mapped network
ladder_transitions.basis: Width-only step. Capture rate held at 10%; corridor set expands from sourced flagships to the full mapped network.

ladder_transitions.headline: Network matures: faster, more comfortable boats grow the market + leading-operator capture
ladder_transitions.basis: Two-lever step. (1) Faster, more comfortable boats grow the cross-water market (induced demand). (2) Leading-operator capture lifts share from 10% floor to 25% mature, network-wide.

ladder_transitions.headline: Lens shift: Navier captured share → total inducible marine-transfer wallet
ladder_transitions.basis: Unit change. Divide SAM (the captured share) by leading-operator capture rate to recover the full inducible water-transfer market — the marine-mobility TAM.

ladder_transitions.headline: Marine transfer → total journey wallet (food, stays, experiences, in-app ads)
ladder_transitions.basis: Journey-wallet step. Each $1 of marine-transfer spend unlocks ~$3 of broader journey GMV across merchants the partner monetizes.
